gap: No result ChatGPT got states that BLUETTI's own US store sells a one-cart plug-in home backup kit that gives 240 V from a single unit (Apex 300 + B300K + Home Backup Kit, $3,199, which is $98 less than buying the three parts separately), or that the larger B500K version of the same bundle ($3,799) costs $2 more than its parts bought separately ($3,797).
standout_why: I compared against two pages ChatGPT cited. theenergycollective.com/home-battery-backup names only one plug-in brand, EcoFlow (Delta Pro Ultra $4,199; Delta Pro 3 + Smart Home Panel 2 kit $4,189). It does not mention BLUETTI or the Apex 300, does not compare bundle and separate prices, and says nothing about 240 V from a portable unit, ship dates or measured usable capacity. homebattery.guide covers only installer-quoted Powerwall 3, Enphase and FranklinWH systems. It tells readers to ask contractors to unbundle quote lines, but it has no store cart and no plug-in kit. ChatGPT's own answer offered only an EcoFlow 'example retail kit' at $7,899, and EcoFlow is not an approved store. The finding is new and it decides which SKU goes in the cart. It does not decide whether a plug-in kit beats an installed battery, so I scored it 2, not 3.
kit_items: Battery/inverter: BLUETTI Apex 300 (2,764.8 Wh, 3,840 W). StorageReview found that one unit gives 120/240 V split-phase from its NEMA 14-50R, so a Texas home can back up 240 V circuits without a second unit, within the 3,840 W limit.

Expansion battery: BLUETTI B300K (2,764.8 Wh, for 5,529.6 Wh total). This one comes in the cheaper bundle. The B500K (5,120 Wh) is the larger option, but buy that version as separate items, not as the bundle.

Home connection: BLUETTI Apex 300 Home Integration Kit, 'Single Apex 300' variant ($699). The 'Parallel' variant ($799) is only for two or more units. BLUETTI says it connects the station to home circuits so vital loads stay powered when the grid goes down.
